summaries.Good news: A pancreatic cancer drug is doubling patient survival, an armless racing driver is breaking barriers at 110 mph, and critical conservation work is thriving through community leadership and eco-tourism.
summaries.Ideas: MIT's Innovators Under 35 showcase breakthrough thinkers solving energy recycling in chips, democratizing steel production, and reversing age-related blindness—while Meta's new AI agent promises to automate digital life at scale.
summaries.Technology: Autonomous vehicles are proving their safety case, 3D-printed housing reaches European scale, and nature-inspired robotics (robotic fish and manta rays) are swimming into practical applications.
summaries.Design: Philadelphia's new arena honors the Spectrum's legacy, a mobility device gives elderly travelers confidence, and browser-based architectural modeling finally brings collaborative design to 3D—while sustainable materials like bio-based pushchairs and upcycled terrazzo gain ground.

items.title: FDA Immediately Approves Drug That’s Doubling Lifespan for Late Pancreatic Cancer Patients
items.snippet: Pancreatic cancer has long been a death sentence, and a rapid one at that, but a new two-a-day pill has seen patients live twice as long even after chemotherapy fails. “Surviving” cancer refers to living more than 5 years post-diagnosis. items.line: A breakthrough pancreatic cancer pill is giving patients twice the survival time, restoring hope to one of the deadliest diagnoses.
